exposure: Ultrasound type (Type I vs. Type II)
Type IIa (poor or no vascularity) vs. Type IIb (rich vascularity)
Type Ia (< 8 weeks) vs. Type Ib (≥ 8 weeks)
cohort: Patients diagnosed with cesarean scar pregnancy or cervical pregnancy between February 2014 and May 2018
finding: The study found a positive correlation between ultrasound categories and treatment methods for intrauterine ectopic pregnancies, suggesting that ultrasound features can guide treatment decisions.
